answer: Sybil resistance uses a slashable identity trellis: each agent locks a bond and needs two bonded peers to vouch, so a fake army must grow a connected trellis of fresh collateral, not just mint cheap keys. Payouts scale with the square root of staked reputation, so splitting into raven copies multiplies bonds but barely raises influence. Proof that two nodes share one wallet or attestation slashes their umber stake and ejects both. The attacker pays quadratically per extra vote and risks losing all bonds at once, making takeover far costlier than honest work.
